chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayyoub al-Khazzaz, from Durays al-Kunasi, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the testimony of the people of the religions (non-Muslims), is it permissible upon a man from other than their religion? So he (peace be upon him) said: No, except that others cannot be found in that situation. So if others cannot be found, their testimonies are permissible regarding the bequest, because it is not correct for the right of a Muslim person to go away, and his bequest would not be invalidated.
ai.seo_question: When is the testimony of non-Muslims valid in Shia Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of 'idtirar' (necessity) in Islamic testimony, where the testimony of non-Muslims is generally rejected but becomes valid when no Muslim witnesses are available to prevent the loss of a Muslim's right. It specifically addresses the context of bequests (wasiyyah), emphasizing that the preservation of property rights takes precedence over the strict exclusion of non-Muslims in their absence. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly view that the invalidity of non-Muslim testimony is not absolute but contingent upon the availability of qualified Muslim witnesses.
